ctx.x: That's great. So after the Paramount Hotel Grill was it the same band you took into the Park Central Hotel? You said you didn't go out of New York.

No. That band more or less fell -- Billy Gussack was the drummer. That band more or less fell apart. We went up and we played the New Kenmore Hotel in Albany, and then we went out to Dayton, Ohio, and Columbus, and the band just folded. We didn't have enough exposure to sustain ourselves and it came apart. The band at the Park

Central was an entirely different band, and we were there for six months. It was a long engagement. Ozzie Nelson had the job, and his manager, a fellow by the name of Milton Romer, took a liking to me and he said, 'You get a band together and we'll put you in here for one night. Ozzie's got a one nighter they're going to let him out for, and if you make a good impression we'll see about getting you in to follow him, you know, for the summer, the spring and the summer.' And fortunately, I guess I got the right…
